article.title: Alcance entre cuantificación universal y negación en mandarín
article.part: Información y discurso avanzado — 信息與進階篇章
article.chapter: Tema, foco, elipsis y cadenas referenciales — 主題、焦點、省略與指稱鏈

claims.summary: For the universal-quantifier and negation interaction discussed by Zhou and Crain, universal > negation corresponds to a ‘none’ reading and negation > universal to a ‘not all’ reading.

claims.sectionKey: Un estudio sobre comprensión infantil y adulta
claims.summary: In Zhou and Crain’s Mandarin experiments, adults accepted only the designated surface-scope readings of the tested sentences, while children accepted both surface- and inverse-scope scenarios.

The study tested particular universal-quantifier and negation constructions, including mei-pi ma dou... and bushi mei-pi ma dou..., and does not establish a blanket translation rule for every surface sequence 都不 and 不都.

links.notes: Defines the two readings as universal-over-negation (none) and negation-over-universal (not all).

locator.section: Abstract, p. 973; §§ 6–8, pp. 984–987; author-version PDF pp. 1, 13–14, 24

links.notes: Reports the tested Mandarin examples and the experimental result: children accepted both readings; adults only the surface-scope scenarios.

locator.section: Abstract and examples (9)–(10), pp. 973–976; author-version PDF pp. 1, 4–6

links.notes: The study specifies particular mei-pi ma constructions, including one with dou meiyou and another beginning bushi; it does not evaluate the exact pair of broad standalone templates asserted by the former entry.
